Janata Jute Mills Ltd. & Sadat Jute Industries Ltd., flagship concerns of the AkijBashir Group, are the largest private-sector jute manufacturer and exporter in Bangladesh. With a proud legacy since 1967, our state-of-the-art facilities in Faridpur, Narsingdi, and Cumilla produce high-quality jute yarn, twine, and diversified products—exporting to nearly 145 countries across the globe. This extensive international footprint reflects our strong market leadership, global trust, and commitment to excellence. Position Summary
The Officer Medical Warehouse will be responsible for the effective management, storage, handling, monitoring, and distribution of medicines, medical supplies, medical consumables, equipment and other health commodities for the Primary Health Care Centre (PHCC) under the Rohingya Response in Cox’s Bazar.
The position holder will ensure that all health commodities are received, stored, cold chain management, recorded, issued, and distributed in accordance with organizational policies, donor requirements, applicable national regulations, and approved medical supply chain procedures.
The Medical Warehouse Officer will maintain accurate inventory records, monitor stock levels and expiry dates, apply appropriate stock rotation principles, prevent stock-outs, overstocking, losses, damage, and wastage, and ensure proper storage conditions for medical commodities.
The position holder will work closely with the Med-log team, Clinical Coordinator, Medical Officer Lead, Medical Officers, Nursing team, Midwifery team, Laboratory, Nutrition, Procurement, Supply Chain, Finance, and other relevant teams to ensure the timely availability of essential medical supplies and commodities required for PHCC service delivery.

Ensure proper receipt, storage, handling, and issuance of medicines, medical supplies, consumables, and other health commodities.
Maintain accurate and up-to-date inventory records.
Monitor stock levels to ensure the continuous availability of essential health commodities.

Ensure proper documentation of all stock movements.

Ensure appropriate documentation of all received commodities.
Coordinate with Procurement and Supply Chain regarding discrepancies or damaged items.
Ensure received commodities are properly recorded and stored.
Storage & Warehouse Organization
Ensure medical commodities are stored safely, securely, and systematically.
Maintain clean, organized, and accessible warehouse conditions.
Ensure appropriate shelving, stacking, labeling, and segregation of commodities.
Store medicines and medical commodities according to manufacturer recommendations and organizational procedures.
Monitor and maintain appropriate storage conditions, including temperature and other environmental requirements.
Maintain temperature monitoring records where applicable.
Ensure appropriate separation of expired, damaged, quarantined, returned, or unusable items.
Ensure restricted and sensitive commodities are stored securely according to applicable procedures.
Maintain appropriate access control and warehouse security.
Stock Rotation & Expiry Management
Apply FEFO (First Expiry, First Out) principles for medicines and other applicable health commodities.
Monitor expiry dates regularly.
Maintain an updated expiry tracking system.
Identify items approaching expiry and communicate them promptly to relevant teams.
Support redistribution or appropriate utilization of short-expiry items according to organizational procedures.
Ensure expired commodities are immediately segregated and clearly labelled.
Prevent the issuance or use of expired medical commodities.
Support appropriate disposal of expired or damaged commodities in accordance with approved procedures and environmental requirements.
Stock Issuance & Distribution
Process approved requests for medicines, medical supplies, and other health commodities.
Ensure commodities are issued accurately and according to authorized requests.
Prepare issue vouchers, stock transfer documents, and other relevant documentation.
Ensure receiving personnel acknowledge receipt of issued commodities.
Maintain accurate records of all stock issued and transferred.
Coordinate the timely distribution of commodities to the Pharmacy, Laboratory, PHCC service points, and other authorized locations.
Monitor distribution requirements and support timely replenishment.
Ensure appropriate accountability during stock movement and transfer.
Stock Monitoring & Forecasting Support
Monitor stock consumption and utilization trends.
Identify fast-moving, slow-moving, critical, and non-moving items.
Provide timely information regarding low stock, potential stock-outs, overstocking, and excess commodities.
Support stock forecasting and replenishment planning.
Prepare and share regular stock status reports.
Coordinate with Pharmacy, clinical teams, and Supply Chain regarding anticipated commodity requirements.
Support the preparation of procurement requests and replenishment plans.
Highlight critical supply gaps that may affect healthcare service delivery.
Cold Chain & Temperature-Controlled Commodities
Ensure appropriate storage and monitoring of temperature-sensitive medical commodities, where applicable.
Maintain temperature monitoring records according to organizational procedures.
Identify and report temperature excursions or cold chain breaches immediately.
Support appropriate corrective action when storage conditions fall outside required ranges.
Ensure appropriate handling and transportation of temperature-sensitive commodities.
Coordinate with relevant technical teams regarding cold chain equipment maintenance and requirements.
Medical Commodity Accountability
Ensure accountability and traceability of all medical commodities.
Maintain accurate documentation for receipts, issues, transfers, returns, adjustments, and disposals.
Support regular stock reconciliation.
Investigate and report losses, damages, discrepancies, or suspected misuse.
Ensure stock adjustments are made only with appropriate authorization.
Maintain supporting documents for all inventory transactions.
Support internal and external audits, stock verification, and donor monitoring visits.
Quality Assurance & Compliance
Ensure warehouse operations comply with organizational policies and standard operating procedures.
Follow applicable national regulations related to medical commodities and warehouse management.
Ensure compliance with donor and programme requirements.
Maintain proper documentation for audit and accountability purposes.
Support implementation of recommendations from audits, monitoring visits, and stock inspections.
Identify warehouse management gaps and recommend improvements.
Promote good storage and distribution practices.
Infection Prevention, Safety & Security
Maintain cleanliness and appropriate hygiene within the medical warehouse.
Follow organizational health and safety procedures.
Ensure safe handling of medical commodities.
Support proper segregation and storage of hazardous or special items according to approved procedures.
Ensure fire safety equipment is available and accessible.
Report safety hazards, damaged storage facilities, or security concerns promptly.
Maintain restricted access to the warehouse.
Ensure warehouse conditions minimize risks of contamination, damage, theft, or loss.
Coordination with Pharmacy & Clinical Teams
Work closely with the Pharmacy team to ensure the availability of essential medicines and medical commodities.
Coordinate with Medical Officers, Nursing, Midwifery, Laboratory, Nutrition, and other teams regarding commodity requirements.
Support timely replenishment of PHCC service points.
Communicate stock availability, shortages, and supply constraints to relevant teams.
Participate in relevant stock coordination and supply planning meetings.

Ensure proper filing and safe storage of warehouse documents.
Maintain electronic inventory records where applicable.
Ensure timely updating of stock records.
Maintain accurate documentation for expired, damaged, returned, or disposed commodities.
Ensure confidentiality and security of relevant programme and inventory information.

Prepare and submit daily, weekly, monthly, and other required warehouse and stock reports.
Prepare stock status reports and consumption summaries.
Report low stock levels, stock-outs, short-expiry items, and other supply concerns promptly.
Support the preparation of donor, programme, and internal inventory reports.
Provide accurate inventory information to relevant teams and management.
Ensure reports are complete, accurate, and submitted on time.
Physical Stock Counts & Inventory Reconciliation
Conduct regular physical stock counts according to organizational procedures.
Participate in monthly, quarterly, and annual stock verification exercises.
Reconcile physical stock with stock records.
Investigate and report stock discrepancies.
Prepare stock adjustment requests where necessary and obtain appropriate authorization.
Support internal and external audit processes.
Ensure corrective actions are implemented to address identified inventory management gaps.

Maintain updated knowledge of organizational warehouse procedures and medical commodity management standards.

Identify opportunities to improve warehouse efficiency and inventory control.
Support implementation of improved stock management systems and procedures.
Promote accountability, accuracy, and continuous improvement in warehouse operations.
16. Emergency Preparedness & Humanitarian Response

Support rapid mobilization and distribution of medical commodities during disease outbreaks, fires, natural disasters, mass casualty incidents, and other humanitarian emergencies.
Maintain awareness of emergency stock requirements.

Ensure essential commodities remain available during emergency situations.
Remain flexible to undertake additional responsibilities based on emergency and programme requirements.

The position holder needs to visit houses at least 3 days a week.
The position holder will work closely with the CHW Supervisor, Clinical Coordinator, Medical Officer Lead, Medical Officers, Nursing Team, Midwifery Team, IPC, Surveillance, Nutrition, MHPSS, Protection, WASH, and other relevant teams to strengthen the link between the community and PHCC services and promote timely access to healthcare.

Accountable to: Deputy Project Coordinator

CHW Supervision & Team Support
Provide day-to-day supervision and support to assigned Community Health Workers (CHWs).
Support the implementation of CHW work plans and daily activities.
Conduct regular supportive supervision and field monitoring.
Provide guidance and practical support to CHWs during community activities.
Monitor CHW attendance, punctuality, and assigned responsibilities.
Facilitate community to capture lesson learnt, case stories.
Support appropriate allocation of CHWs to designated communities or areas.
Escalate significant performance or operational concerns to the CHW Supervisor.
Promote teamwork, accountability, professionalism, and respectful behaviour among CHWs.
Community Health Education & Promotion
Build capacity of the CHWs on the messages to share with the community.
Support CHWs in conducting community health education and awareness activities.
Ensure CHWs provide accurate, approved, and culturally appropriate health messages.
Promote key health topics, including:
o Personal hygiene and handwashing.
o Safe water and sanitation.
o Communicable disease prevention.
o Maternal and child health.
o Nutrition.
o Immunization awareness.
o Prevention and early identification of common diseases.
o Infection Prevention and Control (IPC).
o Health-seeking behaviour.
o Appropriate use of PHCC services.
Support community awareness sessions and group discussions.
Ensure health education messages are consistent with approved organizational and health sector guidance.
Community Mobilization & PHCC Linkage
Support community mobilization to promote access to PHCC services.
Strengthen communication between the community and PHCC.
Support CHWs in identifying barriers to healthcare access.
Encourage appropriate and timely health-seeking behaviour.
Promote awareness of available PHCC services.
Support dissemination of information regarding service availability and schedules.
Support community mobilization during health campaigns and special activities.
Communicate community concerns and feedback to relevant PHCC teams.
Identification & Referral of Patients
Support CHWs in identifying individuals with health concerns requiring further assessment.
Ensure CHWs recognize basic danger signs and referral criteria according to approved guidance.
Support timely referral of sick or vulnerable individuals to the PHCC or other appropriate services.
Ensure CHWs do not provide clinical diagnosis or treatment beyond their approved scope.
Support communication between CHWs and PHCC teams regarding urgent referrals.
Follow up on referred individuals where appropriate.
Monitor referral completion and identify barriers.
Ensure appropriate documentation of referrals.
Follow-Up of Referred Cases
Support CHWs in following up on individuals referred to PHCC services.
Encourage patients and caregivers to complete recommended referrals.
Identify barriers preventing individuals from accessing healthcare.
Communicate significant follow-up concerns to the relevant supervisor or clinical team.
Maintain appropriate referral and follow-up records.
Support continuity of care through appropriate community-level follow-up.
Ensure patient confidentiality during follow-up activities.
Disease Surveillance & Community Alerts
Support CHWs in identifying and reporting unusual health events.
Promote timely reporting of suspected disease outbreaks and unusual health concerns.
Support CHWs in identifying potential clusters of illness or unusual increases in cases.
Ensure community health alerts are communicated promptly to the CHW Supervisor and Surveillance team.
Support event-based and community-based surveillance activities as assigned.
Assist with community-level follow-up during public health alerts.
Maintain confidentiality and avoid spreading unverified information.
Support for Outbreak Response
Support community health activities during disease outbreaks and public health emergencies.
Assist in disseminating approved outbreak prevention and control messages.
Support community mobilization during outbreak response activities.
Coordinate with Surveillance and IPC teams as required.
Support CHWs in identifying and reporting suspected cases according to approved procedures.
Assist in promoting appropriate health-seeking and referral behaviour.
Participate in emergency response activities as assigned.
Community-Based Infection Prevention & Control
Support CHWs in promoting key community-level IPC practices.
Promote hand hygiene and respiratory hygiene.
Support health education on prevention of communicable diseases.
Disseminate approved information regarding infection prevention.
Coordinate with the IPC team regarding community IPC messages.
Support community awareness activities during outbreaks.
Ensure CHWs provide consistent and accurate IPC information.
Community Feedback & Accountability
Support the collection of community feedback regarding health services.
Identify common concerns, barriers, and suggestions from community members.
Communicate relevant feedback to the CHW Supervisor and appropriate PHCC teams.
Support appropriate follow-up of community concerns.
Promote respectful and responsive communication with community members.
Support awareness of available feedback and complaint mechanisms.
Ensure sensitive concerns are handled according to organizational procedures.
Coordination with Multidisciplinary Teams
Work closely with the CHW Supervisor and relevant PHCC teams.
Coordinate with Medical, Nursing, Midwifery, Nutrition, MHPSS, IPC, Surveillance, WASH, and Protection teams.
Support integrated health promotion and community outreach activities.
Communicate community-level health concerns to relevant service providers.
Participate in coordination meetings when required.
Support referral and follow-up between community and facility services.
Promote effective teamwork and communication.
CHW Training & Capacity Building
Support orientation of newly recruited CHWs.
Assist in organizing refresher training sessions.
Provide regular on-the-job coaching and mentoring.
Support training on:
o Health promotion.
o Community engagement.
o Referral procedures.
o Recognition of danger signs.
o Basic disease prevention.
o IPC.
o Community surveillance.
o Confidentiality and professional conduct.
o Safeguarding and PSEA.
Identify CHW knowledge and skills gaps.
Maintain training and coaching records.
Monitoring & Field Supervision
Conduct regular field monitoring of CHW activities.
Observe health education sessions and community engagement activities.
Monitor the quality and accuracy of health messages.
Review CHW activity records and reports.
Verify selected reported activities where required.
Provide constructive feedback to CHWs.
Document monitoring findings and follow up on improvement actions.
Report significant issues to the CHW Supervisor.
Data Collection, Documentation & Reporting
Support CHWs in maintaining accurate activity records.
Collect and review CHW activity reports.
Check reports for completeness and consistency.
Support compilation of daily, weekly, and monthly CHW activity data.
Maintain records of referrals, follow-up, health education sessions, and community activities.
Support preparation of routine reports.
Report significant community health concerns promptly.
Maintain confidentiality of community and patient information.
Supplies & Materials Management
Support monitoring of CHW supplies and health education materials.
Ensure CHWs have access to approved IEC/BCC materials.
Monitor the appropriate use and distribution of materials.
Maintain basic records of materials issued to CHWs.
Identify shortages and report them promptly.
Support replenishment of approved materials.
Ensure proper accountability of organizational resources.
Safeguarding, PSEA & Protection
Promote safeguarding and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) among CHWs.
Ensure CHWs understand and follow organizational safeguarding policies.
Promote respectful and non-discriminatory engagement with community members.
Ensure CHWs maintain confidentiality and professional boundaries.
Identify and report safeguarding concerns through approved reporting mechanisms.
Promote awareness of available complaint and feedback mechanisms.
Ensure community activities are conducted safely and respectfully.
Emergency Preparedness & Humanitarian Response
Support CHW preparedness for humanitarian emergencies.
Assist in mobilizing CHWs during disease outbreaks, fires, natural disasters, or other emergencies.
Support rapid dissemination of approved emergency health messages.
Assist in identifying vulnerable individuals requiring support.
Support community-level emergency preparedness activities.
Remain flexible to undertake additional responsibilities based on programme requirements.
Additional Job Responsibilities
The duties and responsibilities outlined above are not exhaustive. The role holder may be required to undertake additional duties reasonably related to their qualifications, skills, and experience, based on programme and operational requirements.
Safeguarding
The post holder is required to perform all duties in accordance with the organization's safeguarding, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), child safeguarding, anti-harassment, code of conduct, and other relevant policies and procedures.
Equal Opportunity
The organization is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from qualified candidates regardless of gender, age, disability, ethnicity, religion, or other status.
Health and Safety
The post holder is required to carry out all duties in accordance with organizational Health, Safety, Security, Infection Prevention and Control (IPC), and other relevant policies and procedures.
Salary & Benefits

Position overview:	
The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN) Officer provides technical leadership for Room to Read’s integrated Foundational Literacy and Numeracy program, including Literacy, Numeracy, and School Library components, for the early grades. The position oversees the quality and fidelity of program implementation, leads teacher professional development, provides technical supervision and capacity building to FLN Facilitators, and supports effective use of instructional, assessment and library resources.
The FLN Officer works closely with the Field Manager to ensure effective planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting, and coordinates with government education officials and Room to Read’s RM&E, Finance, Administration and Technical teams to strengthen program quality, scale and sustainability.
The FLN Officer reports to the Field Manager and provides technical supervision to FLN Facilitators. The position also supports annual planning, budgeting, implementation tracking, data analysis, reporting and field-level problem solving.
Duties and responsibilities:
A. Technical Leadership and Program Quality
Provide technical leadership to ensure that Literacy and Numeracy instructional approaches, implementation routines, School Library practices and quality standards are consistently understood and implemented across assigned schools.
Oversee the quality, fidelity and effectiveness of FLN implementation across the assigned portfolio of schools and ensure alignment with approved program design and standards.
Identify and analyze program design, implementation and quality issues and facilitate timely, solution-oriented responses in coordination with the Field Manager and Country Office Technical Team.
Provide technical guidance to Facilitators, schools and teachers on effective instructional practices, coaching approaches, assessment use, teaching and learning materials, and integration of library-based reading opportunities.
Provide technical inputs into the development and refinement of FLN instructional materials, teacher guides, training modules, coaching tools, assessment tools, library resources and digital content in coordination with relevant technical teams.
B. Teacher Professional Development and Facilitator Capacity Building
Lead the planning and delivery of technical training for teachers, Head Teachers, FLN Facilitators, government officials and other relevant stakeholders, ensuring alignment with program standards and approved plans.
Lead the induction, orientation, continuous capacity building and technical coaching of FLN Facilitators to ensure they have the knowledge, skills and tools required for effective school-level coaching and implementation support.
Provide ongoing technical supervision to FLN Facilitators in their school coaching, classroom observation, implementation support, data collection and engagement with Head Teachers, teachers and government stakeholders.
Accompany Facilitators periodically during school visits to observe the quality of coaching and implementation support, provide feedback, model effective practices and identify capacity-building needs.
Supervise and support the performance of FLN Facilitators through regular review, coaching, performance feedback and professional development, in coordination with the Field Manager.
Develop and maintain a resource pool of Master Trainers and technical resource persons in foundational literacy, numeracy, instructional practices, coaching and related FLN areas.
C. School Library and Reading Integration
Provide technical oversight to ensure that the School Library component is effectively integrated into the broader FLN program to promote children’s reading habits, enjoyment of reading, access to quality storybooks and opportunities to read at school and at home.
Guide Facilitators and schools on effective use of storytelling, read-alouds, book sharing, independent reading, library-based activities and reading-at-home practices as complementary opportunities to strengthen literacy development.
Provide technical input into library-related training, tools, guidance and sustainability mechanisms and promote integration of reading culture within school and community practices.
D. Implementation Supervision and Quality Assurance
Ensure that FLN Facilitators effectively conduct school visits, teacher coaching, classroom observations, materials-use monitoring, library support, family/community engagement and implementation follow-up in accordance with program standards.
Review and triangulate classroom observation, coaching, program fidelity, assessment, materials-use and library-use data to assess implementation quality and identify areas requiring additional support.
Ensure that schools receive instructional materials, student materials, assessment resources, storybooks and other program resources in a timely manner and that their use is consistent with program design.
E. Data, Evidence and Learning
Analyze FLN implementation, monitoring, coaching, assessment, materials-use and library-use data generated from the field to identify trends, implementation gaps, emerging issues and opportunities for improvement.
Review data submitted by FLN Facilitators for completeness, accuracy, consistency and quality, and coordinate with the RM&E team to resolve data-quality issues.
Ensure timely and accurate monthly, quarterly and annual data compilation, analysis and reporting within agreed systems and timelines.
Work with the Field Manager and relevant technical teams to ensure that data and evidence inform programmatic decisions, resource allocation, implementation strategies and technical support.
Contribute to or lead action research, implementation research, pilots and learning activities related to FLN, as assigned.
F. Government Engagement and System Strengthening
Support coordination with district and Upazila-level government education officials on FLN implementation, monitoring, review, training and capacity-building activities.
Represent Room to Read in relevant government meetings, technical discussions and committees related to foundational literacy, numeracy, early grade learning, school libraries and primary education.
Engage government stakeholders to promote effective implementation, institutionalization, scale-up and sustainability of FLN practices within government primary schools.
Support Facilitators in maintaining constructive school-level communication with government stakeholders while taking responsibility for higher-level technical coordination and issue resolution.
G. Planning, Coordination and Reporting
Support the Field Manager in developing the annual FLN plan of action and budget, covering professional development, school support, materials, monitoring, library activities, government engagement and other program priorities.
Provide regular feedback to the Country Office Technical Team on field implementation, technical challenges, Facilitator and teacher capacity needs, design issues and emerging learning.
Participate in regular meetings with the Field Manager, Facilitators and relevant technical teams to review progress and agree on priorities and follow-up actions.
H. Documentation, Learning and Sustainability
Ensure systematic documentation of FLN implementation, Facilitator supervision, training, coaching quality, government engagement, monitoring findings, library integration and follow-up actions.
Identify, document and share best practices, innovations, implementation challenges, lessons learned and promising approaches with the Field Manager and relevant technical teams.
Support development of sustainability and scale mechanisms that enable teachers, Head Teachers and government stakeholders to continue effective FLN and reading practices beyond Room to Read’s direct support.
Participate in other activities required to fulfill the objectives of the organization.

Position overview: The Field Manager (FM) provides overall leadership and management of the Room to Read Bangladesh field office and its program portfolio, ensuring effective, high-quality, cost-efficient and timely implementation of the annual plan and achievement of program targets.

Build and maintain strategic relationships with government agencies, NGO partners, education stakeholders and local institutions to support program implementation, scale and sustainability.
Support engagement with government stakeholders to strengthen government ownership, institutionalization and sustainability of Room to Read-supported approaches.
Coordinate with relevant Country Office teams to support donor visits, partner visits, external events and other stakeholder engagements in the field.

Introduction: Solidaridad (www.solidaridadnetwork.org) is a global network organization working to build sustainable, resource-efficient, and inclusive supply chains. Solidaridad fosters smallholder and worker empowerment by co-creating scalable, economically viable solutions in agricultural and industrial landscapes alongside governments, businesses, and local communities.
In coastal southwest Bangladesh, Solidaridad is implementing the extension phase of the ‘Sustainable Agriculture, Food Security and Livelihoods for Integrated Water Resources Management (SAFAL for IWRM)’ project. Having successfully revitalized 92 micro-watersheds, improving agricultural productivity and livelihoods for over 91,000 farming households, the project now focuses on institutionalizing watershed-based governance to ensure equitable water distribution, resource efficiency, and climate resilience. To bridge community-led water management with private sector-led supply chains and advanced agricultural innovations, the project aims to establish a bankable, commercial water-climate-agriculture nexus approach that transitions micro-watersheds into self-sustaining, commercially viable Agri-Business Hubs.
Solidaridad Network Asia is seeking Programme Officers – Ecosystem Regeneration to provide technical and operational leadership for the field-level implementation of the Ecosystem Regeneration component. Under the strategic guidance of the Manager – Ecosystem Regeneration, the Programme Officer will support and guide Field Extension Officers in strengthening farmers’ capacities on ecosystem regeneration practices, developing farmer entrepreneurs within the supply chain, and promoting the adoption of digital advisory systems. The position will also contribute to systematic documentation of field experiences, good practices, lessons learned, and emerging innovations to support programme learning and scale-up.
Overall purpose of the Role: The Programme Officer – Ecosystem Regeneration will provide technical and operational support to promote and scale climate-smart and regenerative agriculture solutions at the field level. The role will facilitate collaboration among farmers, farmer-owned enterprises, private-sector actors, technology providers, and government stakeholders to promote climate-resilient seeds, regenerative farming practices, protected cultivation, micro-irrigation, bio-inputs, digital advisory services, and energy-efficient post-harvest solutions.
The position will also support the development of farmer entrepreneurs, strengthen localized value-chain and market linkages, and promote integrated water-agriculture-climate solutions to improve smallholder productivity, resource efficiency, resilience, and commercial viability. In addition, the role will contribute to strengthening local water governance, capacity building, knowledge management, and policy engagement.
Employment Type: Project-based fixed-term
Reports to: Manager – Ecosystem Regeneration
Supervises: No direct reports; provides technical supervision
Duty Station: Khulna/Jashore, with frequent field travel
Key Responsibilities
Promotion of Climate-Smart and regenerative farming practices:
Identify and formalize partnerships with premium seed companies for field demonstration of high-yielding, water-stress and saline-tolerant hybrid varieties.
Jointly select suitable seed varieties with partners through structured meetings/workshops.
Support partners to identify and train interested farmers and establish demonstration plots.
Monitor demo-plot performance and organize field days and cross-visits to share results.
Farmer Capacity Building on Regenerative agriculture, land and water use planning, protected cultivation systems, and micro-irrigation.
Establish collaboration with EKN-supported projects and private-sector actors piloting low-cost protected agriculture (net houses/polytunnels.
Mobilize farmers/Entrepreneurs in the suitable MWS and facilitate promotion of selected low-cost protected agriculture facilities (Farmers and Entrepreneurs).
Capacity building of farmers on climate-smart and Regenerative agriculture systems, cluster-level land and water use planning, and protected cultivation.
Establishment of Demo plots on regenerative practices and learning sharing.
Scale the commercial production of vermicompost and adoption of biological crop protection techniques (pheromone traps)
Select farmer entrepreneurs in the vegetable-intensive MWSs for establishing a commercial vermicompost production plant, provide capacity-building training, branding and marketing support.
Support selected Farmers Entrepreneurs to establish and operate a vermicompost production plant.
Establish partnerships with relevant private sectors and connect the FOE with the private sector to make biological protection materials and technologies available to farmers.
Onboard new technology providers and local private investors to introduce energy-efficient logistics packaging and distribution
Partnership with technology providers and local private investors to introduce energy-efficient logistics packaging and distribution.
Optimize watersheds and land through advanced micro-irrigation practices to enable year-round cultivation of high-value crops (vegetables, fish and dairy).
Pilot digital advisory tools to monitor services to track crop water stress, salinity, and detect soil nutrient deficiency in real-time to de-risk smallholder investment.
Establish a partnership with Private Sector Company/Organization promoting a proven remote sensing digital advisory system.
Build awareness among farmers on the advisory system and provide digital advisory services to the selected number of farmers.
Co-design and co-create collective actions for developing the water-agriculture-climate nexus in collaboration with public-private and the embassy-supported initiatives
Establish collaborative partnerships with the private sector, public sector, and embassy-supported projects and define strategy for Collaboration.
Promote integrated climate-smart aquaculture practices among the farmers of selected MWS through Demo plots, result-sharing sessions, cross-visits, etc. (YY Super male Tilapia, Seabus and Vannamei shrimp).
Institutionalization and Strengthening of Local Water Governance
Facilitate the formalization and organizational strengthening of farmers’ collectives/MWCs, including registration, governance systems, MoUs with Union Parishads, and alignment with local government structures.
Support sustainable O&M financing through membership subscriptions, water-use fees, fund generation, regular MWC meetings, and continuous mentoring/backstopping.
Coordinate with government authorities, Union Parishads, Upazila-level IWRM Committees, farmers’ organizations, and other stakeholders to strengthen community-led water governance.
Capacity Building, Knowledge Management and Policy Engagement
Coordinate capacity-building initiatives on governance, business management, and financial literacy, including development of training modules and facilitation of training programmes.
Document and synthesize programme learning, good practices, and evidence into knowledge products and policy papers in collaboration with technical experts and stakeholders.
Organize field visits, workshops, roundtables, and policy dialogues to disseminate learning and promote integration and scaling of the SAFAL IWRM model within relevant government policies and programmes.
Competitive compensation package aligned with Solidaridad Asia’s pay structures and Service Rules. Benefits include Provident Fund, Gratuity, Festival Bonus, and Medical Insurance coverage per organizational policy

Identify and propose relevant research and study areas, conduct, or contribute to research as required, and oversee data collection and analysis.
Develop and provide technical and policy guidance to relevant team and contribute to the design, adaptation, and dissemination of relevant policies, standards, and technical approaches.
Ensure effective knowledge and experience capitalisation, strengthen sectoral approaches globally, and contribute to the collection and use of scientific evidence. Initiate, pilot, and/or test innovative solutions to address key challenges within the sector.
Contribute to technical learning and knowledge management under the guidance of the Technical Specialist or Project Manager, drawing on evidence, lessons learned, and best practices.

Contribute to the development of a local talent pool within the sector by participating in technical interviews, providing recruitment recommendations, and identifying training, mentoring, and coaching needs.
Communicate and contribute to relevant advocacy messages and initiatives within his/her area of responsibility.
Support the development and drafting of new project content to ensure the continuity, expansion, and scaling-up of projects within his/her technical area of expertise.
Support community members in identifying their needs and goals, developing action plans, and gaining insight into their concerns and available coping strategies.
Support relevant team to Identify individuals requiring specialized mental health or other services and refer to psychologists, psychiatrists, health facilities, protection services, or other appropriate service providers, as necessary.

Name of Project: Culturally Aligned Generative AI for Mental Health in Bangladesh
The Field Coordinator will lead day-to-day, site-level implementation of project activities, including community mobilization, stakeholder engagement, and scheduling and logistics for screening, counselling, and courtyard sessions. The role serves as the primary liaison between the community, the field team, and project management; is responsible for monitoring field-level activity, data quality, and progress against the workplan; and manages site-level procurement and billing processes. The Field Coordinator provides logistical and scheduling support to Para-counselors but does not hold a supervisory reporting line over them- Para-counselors report to the Psychologist for clinical supervision.
A) Site Coordination and Community Mobilization
Lead community entry and mobilization activities across the assigned communities (both data-collection and implementation sites).
Plan, organize courtyard sessions and stakeholder engagement sessions in line with project protocols and training.
Coordinate participant recruitment and screening logistics (venue, scheduling, participant flow) in line with site-level targets.
Build and maintain strong relationships with community members and act as the primary point of contact at field level.
B) Team Coordination and Logistical Support
Coordinate daily and weekly activity schedules and site logistics for Para-counselors at the assigned site.
Track activity completion and site-level case flow for monitoring and reporting purposes, flagging logistical or scheduling issues to the Psychologist as needed.
Support onboarding and logistical arrangements for training, screening-tools & other activities.
Liaise with the Psychologist to support tracking of referrals and coordination of complex-case logistics.
C) Stakeholder Engagement and Referral Pathways
Represent the project at community-level coordination meetings with local government, health facilities, and other stakeholders.
Support mapping and maintenance of local referral pathways in coordination with the Psychologist and Project Manager.
Facilitate stakeholder engagement sessions to build community trust and reduce mental health stigma.
D) Data Management, Monitoring and Reporting
Ensure timely and accurate data collection, entry, and reporting from field activities, including screening and session tracking.
Monitor progress against workplan milestones at the site level and flag delays or risks to the Project Manager.
Prepare and submit site-level activity and progress reports.
Support documentation of case stories, good practices, and field-level learnings.
E) Procurement and Billing
Support site-level procurement of goods and services (venues, training materials, refreshments, transport, etc.) in line with SF procurement policy and project budget lines.
Prepare and submit purchase requisitions, vendor quotations/comparative statements, and supporting documents for site-level expenses.
Verify, compile, and process bills, invoices, and payment vouchers for field activities, and route them for timely approval and payment.
Maintain accurate records of site-level expenditures, receipts, and supporting documentation for financial reporting and audit purposes.
Coordinate with the Finance/Admin team at Head Office for fund requests, disbursement, reimbursement, and reconciliation of site-level accounts.
Ensure site-level procurement and billing practices comply with donor and organizational financial guidelines.
F) Other
Support logistics for field visits by project management & relevant stakeholders.
Undertake other duties as assigned, relevant to the role.

• Hands-on experience with Drata or an equivalent GRC/compliance automation platform (Vanta, Secureframe, Sprinto) — including control monitoring, evidence management, and remediation of failing tests.
• Working knowledge of ISO/IEC 27001 audits — direct experience of implementation, internal audit, or certification/surveillance audits, including evidence preparation and liaising with external auditors.
• Strong knowledge of security risk assessment, vulnerability management, and security operations.
• Experience conducting or coordinating penetration testing and reviewing scan results.
• Familiarity with incident response processes and access management.
Professional Certifications (Preferred)
• ISO 27001 Lead Implementer (highly desirable) — for candidates with a Lead Auditor qualification, this is valued only for audit liaison and evidence preparation, given this role's operational (non-auditing) function.
• CISM, CISSP, CRISC, or equivalent security management/risk certification.

• ITIL Foundation (added benefit).
Key Skills & Competencies
• Strong understanding of security governance, standards, frameworks, and controls.
• Ability to interpret and evaluate control evidence and risk documentation.
• Excellent communication skills with the ability to work across technical and non-technical teams, including external consultants and auditors.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.

About the Role
We are seeking a highly skilled Senior IT Security Officer to support the day-to-day management of the Information Security Management System (ISMS), regulatory compliance, and security governance.
This role is critical in ensuring the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of our information assets while maintaining compliance with ISO/IEC 27001:2022, UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, and internal security policies.
You will operate our Drata GRC platform, manage security risks, coordinate vulnerability testing, support incident response, contribute to access governance, and collaborate cross-functionally — working alongside our external vCISO/GRC partner under a clearly defined division of responsibilities. This is a hands-on and strategic role ideal for professionals passionate about security, governance, and continuous improvement.
Key Responsibilities
1. ISMS & Compliance Management (ISO/IEC 27001:2022, UK GDPR, TISAX, ISO 9001)
•Operate the Drata trust management platform, ensuring timely review of failing tests, findings, and KPIs, in coordination with the external GRC partner.
•Maintain audit-ready evidence in Drata for certification and annual surveillance audits.
•Support the implementation, maintenance, and continual improvement of the ISMS.
•Prepare, review, and maintain compliance documentation and audit evidence.
•Support UK GDPR and DPA 2018 compliance activities, supporting the Data Protection Officer (the DPO function remains independent of this role).
•Manage the operational relationship with the GRC platform (Drata) and coordinate with penetration testing vendors, including scheduling, scope confirmation, and remediation tracking within budget guidelines set by the CTO.
2. Security Risk & Asset Management
•Conduct and review information security risk assessments in line with the Risk Assessment Policy.
•Maintain and treat assigned risks as an Information Security Risk Owner.
•Ensure security controls are implemented and monitored across information assets.
•Lead or support periodic user access reviews.
•Support supplier and third-party risk assessments in line with ISO/IEC 27001:2022, including onboarding due diligence, contractual security requirements, and periodic supplier reviews.
3. Vulnerability Management & Penetration Testing
•Coordinate annual penetration tests (internal or external) and event-driven tests following major infrastructure changes.
•Review vulnerability scan results and work with IT and Engineering to remediate risks within policy timescales.
•Monitor emerging threats through advisories, bulletins, and intelligence feeds.
4. Access Control & Authorisation
•Review and endorse system and physical access requests based on least-privilege principles; privileged and restricted-data access requires a second approver (CTO or system owner) in line with segregation-of-duties requirements.
•Review BYOD and remote-working arrangements in line with the Mobile & Teleworking Policy and MDM (Microsoft Intune) enrolment requirements.
5. Incident Response & Security Operations Support
•Investigate and assess incidents, including suspected credential compromise, in accordance with the Incident Response Plan.
•Support security monitoring, detection, and response activities.
•Produce incident reports and ensure corrective actions are logged and tracked through the Continuous Improvement and Non-Conformity process.
6. Disaster Recovery & Business Continuity
•Maintain and update the Disaster Recovery (DR) Plan in collaboration with the Data Protection Officer and the IT Operations Officer.
•Define DR validation criteria, schedule tests, and ensure testing execution and evidence capture.
•Contribute to the wider Business Continuity Plan (BCP), including crisis communication procedures, beyond IT-specific disaster recovery.
7. Internal Audit & Governance
•Prepare evidence and act as auditee for internal and external (certification body) audits; this role does not audit controls it operates, preserving internal audit independence.
•Participate in ISO/IEC 27001 surveillance and recertification audit preparation and audit sessions with the certification body.
•Support governance reporting, metrics, management review inputs, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Vacancy:  1
Age:  At least 30 years
Job Location:  Anywhere in Bangladesh
Salary:  Negotiable
Experience:  
Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Procurement, Business Administration, Logistics, Commerce, or a relevant field.
Professional certification in procurement/supply chain is an advantage.
Experience – Essential
Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in procurement and supply chain management.
Experience in procurement of medical supplies, medicines, equipment, or NGO programme materials is highly desirable.
Experience with procurement documentation, vendor management, inventory coordination, and supply chain tracking.
Desirable
Experience with NGO/INGO or humanitarian programmes, particularly in the Rohingya Response.
Experience working with donor-funded projects and procurement compliance requirements.
Knowledge of ERP/procurement systems, MS Excel, and digital procurement trackers.
Skills & Competencies
Technical Skills
Strong knowledge of procurement and supply chain procedures.
Good understanding of vendor sourcing, quotation analysis, bid evaluation, and contract management.
Strong Excel, data management, documentation, and reporting skills.
Good understanding of inventory and logistics coordination.
Communication & Interpersonal Skills
Strong communication, negotiation, and coordination skills.
Ability to work effectively with suppliers and multidisciplinary teams.
Good written and spoken English and Bangla.
Other Competencies
Strong attention to detail and analytical skills.
Integrity, confidentiality, accountability, and commitment to ethical procurement.
Ability to prioritize multiple tasks and work under pressure.
Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills.
Working Conditions
Based at the assigned PHCC/MCH/field office with regular coordination with warehouse, logistics, finance, programme, and management teams.
May require field visits and travel to project locations, suppliers, warehouses, and programme sites.
Ability to work under pressure and respond to urgent humanitarian procurement requirements.
Duty Station: Work at Office
Reports to: Finance and Admin Coordinator
Accountable to: Project Coordinator
Position Summary
The Sr. Officer – Procurement & Supply Chain will support and oversee procurement and supply chain activities for the PHCC/MCH programme, ensuring timely, transparent, cost-effective, and compliant procurement of medicines, medical supplies, equipment, services, and other programme requirements. The position will coordinate with programme, finance, warehouse, logistics, and management teams to maintain an efficient supply chain in line with organizational policies and donor requirements.
Key Responsibilities
Procurement Planning & Coordination
Prepare and maintain procurement plans based on programme needs, budgets, and approved workplans.
Coordinate with programme, pharmacy, warehouse, logistics, and finance teams to identify procurement requirements.
Ensure timely procurement of goods, services, and supplies to avoid stock-outs and programme disruptions.
Procurement Process Management
Manage RFQs, quotations, bid evaluations, purchase requisitions, purchase orders, and related procurement documentation.
Ensure procurement processes are transparent, competitive, and compliant with organizational policies and donor requirements.
Support vendor selection, evaluation, negotiation, and contracting.
Supplier & Vendor Management
Maintain an updated supplier/vendor database and conduct supplier performance monitoring.
Coordinate with suppliers regarding quotations, delivery schedules, quality, specifications, and payment documentation.
Address procurement-related issues and delays in coordination with relevant teams.
Supply Chain & Inventory Coordination
Coordinate with warehouse and logistics teams to ensure timely receipt, storage, distribution, and tracking of procured items.
Monitor stock levels and support timely replenishment of essential supplies.
Ensure proper documentation and traceability of supplies throughout the supply chain.
Quality, Compliance & Due Diligence
Ensure procured items meet approved specifications, quality standards, and programme requirements.
Conduct appropriate vendor due diligence and maintain required procurement records.
Ensure compliance with procurement policies, donor rules, segregation of duties, and ethical procurement practices.
Procurement Documentation & Record Keeping
Maintain complete procurement files, including requisitions, quotations, comparative statements, approvals, POs, contracts, delivery notes, and invoices.
Ensure proper filing and timely availability of procurement documents for audit and review.
Maintain procurement trackers and databases.
Cost Control & Budget Monitoring
Support cost-effective procurement and value-for-money initiatives.
Monitor procurement expenditures against approved budgets and identify potential budget issues.
Coordinate with Finance to ensure proper documentation and timely processing of supplier payments.
Reporting & Data Management
Prepare regular procurement and supply chain reports, trackers, and status updates.
Monitor procurement lead times, pending orders, supplier performance, and delivery status.
Ensure accurate and timely procurement data for management and donor reporting.
Coordination & Team Support
Work closely with programme, finance, warehouse, pharmacy, logistics, and administration teams.
Provide technical support and guidance to junior procurement/supply chain staff.
Participate in procurement and supply chain meetings and support operational decision-making.
Emergency Preparedness & Humanitarian Response
Support rapid procurement of critical medicines, medical supplies, equipment, and other emergency items.
Maintain readiness for urgent procurement requirements during outbreaks, emergencies, or programme scale-up.
Ensure emergency procurement remains properly documented and compliant with organizational procedures.
Monthly Gross Salary: Negotiable
Bonus and other benefits: 10% of the monthly gross salary.
Other Benefits: Office hours, annual leave, increments, will be provided as per the organizational policy and Recruitment & Human Resource Management Policy of Partners in Health and Development (PHD), subject to project budget availability.
